source.title: signSGD: compressed optimisation for non-convex problems
source.authors: Jeremy Bernstein; Yu-Xiang Wang; K. Azizzadenesheli; Anima Anandkumar

record.tranche_reason: Reports the effect of optimizer choice on train and test performance and measures gradient/noise density during training, bearing on V4 and V7 using sign-based optimizers and density measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports train/test accuracy for ResNet-50 v2 under SGD, signum and Adam, and measures gradient and noise density for ResNet-20. The CIFAR-10 results and grid-search values are in figures/tables whose layout is flattened; no recoverable separate numerical rows are assigned from those displays. Figure A.2 reports gradient-density measurements at Xavier initialization, but this is not a measure of the trained-network property named in V7.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam, SIGNUM and momentum SGD using held-out image-classification accuracy, bearing on V4. Gradient/noise density and convergence bounds do not test V7 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's generalization paraphrase is accurate: SIGNUM resembles Adam, and both trail tuned SGD by about 2 percentage points on ImageNet; the tested weight-decay approaches do not fully close that gap. Add that CIFAR-10 final test performance differs little across optimizers. The paper's main conclusion concerns convergence guarantees and communication-efficient sign-based optimization.
record.recipe_differences: Optimizer benchmark on ImageNet and CIFAR-10 comparing S IGNUM, Adam, and SGD; no random-label experiment or generalization-gap intervention. It measures gradient/noise density, not magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.method_sensitivity: On ImageNet, switching off data augmentation at epoch 95; learning rate and weight decay were tuned on a separate validation split. The text says weight decay was well-tuned for the SGD comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient and stochastic-gradient noise densities remain of similar order and appear coupled during ResNet-20 training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient and noise density covary during training in the tested CIFAR-10 setup.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80, 2018
record.problems: The optimizer comparison on ImageNet reports approximate differences in prose without exact test-accuracy values or uncertainty. The CIFAR-10 final test comparison and hyperparameter sweeps are presented in figures/tables, and their detailed cells are flattened in the supplied text. V7's named sharpness measure is not tested.
record.rows_left_out: No reconstructable numerical rows from Figure 3 or Figures A.3–A.4: the text extraction does not provide exact associated values for each optimizer/condition, and the supplementary grid-search tables are flattened. Figure 1 density values are also not transcribed; the described density trend is recorded as R4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label generalization.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Language benchmarks, comprehensive optimizer-specific tuning, and switching from Adam to SGD. The supplied prose does not establish equal or better adaptive-method training performance.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions and their interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
All: magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization-gap ranking, and comparison with norm/margin measures.

missing.what: Qualitative CIFAR-10 result: final test performance differs little among SGD, SIGNUM and Adam after validation tuning. Numerical figure values are declared left out, but the explicit caption result remains usable.
missing.locator: Figure A.3 caption; Figure A.4 caption for tuning and data split

missing.what: SIGNUM achieves better ImageNet test performance than SGD without weight decay; record this separate comparator condition without inventing exact accuracies.
Neither standard weight decay nor the Loshchilov–Hutter approach fully closed the ImageNet gap with SGD; exact residual gaps and implementation details are not supplied in this passage.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. Validation-grid scores are selection results, not final test accuracies. V7 must be changed from tested_not_extracted to not tested; density and speculative discussion of wider valleys do not measure its claim.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweep past interpolation and test-error trend.
Language benchmarks, broader optimizer tuning comparisons, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adaptation recipes.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, weight perturbation tolerance, comparative norm/margin measures, and the stated CIFAR-10/SVHN gap-ranking relationship.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Resnet-50 v2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD and well-tuned weight decay on ImageNet; report final top-1 test accuracy.
rows.value: not stated; described as about 2% better than S IGNUM and A DAM
rows.note: Authors state the approximate performance difference in prose; no exact accuracy value is stated for this comparison.
rows.check: Valid comparator: SGD with tuned weight decay achieves about 2 percentage points higher test accuracy than Adam and SIGNUM. Epoch 95 marks augmentation removal, not the final measurement.

rows.subject: Resnet-50 v2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with S IGNUM (momentum version of SIGN SGD); initial learning rate and weight decay tuned on a separate validation split.
rows.baseline: SGD with well-tuned weight decay; about 2% higher test accuracy
rows.value: approximately the same as A DAM; about 2% worse than SGD with well-tuned weight decay
rows.note: The authors describe the comparison in prose; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: Change partial to observed: the reported accuracy deficit fully exhibits the optimizer difference named in V4. SIGNUM is treated as part of the adaptive/sign-based family in this paper. Epoch 95 is an intervention time, not the final measurement.

rows.subject: Resnet-50 v2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; figure compares train and test accuracy.
rows.baseline: SGD with well-tuned weight decay; about 2% higher test accuracy
rows.value: approximately the same as S IGNUM; about 2% worse than SGD with well-tuned weight decay
rows.note: The authors describe the comparison in prose; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: Change partial to observed: Adam's approximately 2 percentage point deficit supports V4; equal or better training performance is optional in that version. Epoch 95 is an intervention time, not the final measurement.

rows.subject: Resnet-20
rows.operation_detail: Measured exact mean-gradient density and stochastic-gradient noise density at the beginning of each epoch during training.

conditions.value: 3 repeats for each of 3 different training algorithms

rows.measure: gradient density and variance density, using φ(v) = ||v||₁²/(d||v||₂²)
rows.value: Text states gradient and noise densities are of the same order throughout training and appear coupled; exact values are figure-only.
rows.uncertainty: error bars plotted; numerical uncertainty not stated
rows.note: The text describes the trend but provides no exact measurements. The figure compares algorithms; the reported density relationship is not a measure of the V7 magnitude-aware sharpness or training-test gap.
rows.check: Gradient and noise density cannot establish magnitude-aware sharpness or its relationship to the generalization gap. This row does not test V7.
